Your call.

📚 Today you learned

Opportunity Cost of Idle Cash (Cash Drag)

You've been 100% cash for 14 days since the IQV stop-out, and the market hasn't waited — the S&P's up modestly over that stretch even with today's pullback. That's cash drag: the return your dry powder didn't earn while parked. In forex you rarely felt this, because you were usually in a position or the carry on idle margin was near zero either way. In equities, sitting out during a grind-up period is a real, measurable cost — not just "avoiding risk." The flip side: cash drag is the price of discipline, and it's cheap insurance against forcing a bad entry. The math only turns against you if "waiting for the right setup" quietly becomes "not looking for one." With Buffett Indicator at an all-time extreme, some drag is arguably the correct trade right now — just make sure it's a decision, not inertia.

Also today: Time value of capital — even non-withdrawal accounts have an implicit hurdle rate; cash sitting idle competes against T-bill yields (~5%) as the honest baseline it needs to beat.
